title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Seattle University rituals and recurring events, from first-year welcome markers to spring community celebrations.

cards.title: Ring The Chapel Bell
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: During orientation, add this bell-ringing stop to your first-week plans and photograph the moment with your entering class.
cards.short_summary: A first-year marker that ceremonially begins a student’s time at Seattle U.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies ringing the Chapel Bell during Orientation as an annual tradition for new students.
cards.access_notes: Presented as part of new-student Orientation; check Orientation programming for timing.

cards.title: Sign Your Entering Class Banner
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: Find the entering-class banner during orientation, sign your name clearly, and save a photo before moving on to other welcome events.
cards.short_summary: New students write their names into Seattle U history on their class banner.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists signing an entering class banner as a tradition for new students.
cards.access_notes: Offered through Orientation activities; confirm the current schedule with Orientation Programs.

cards.entity_name: Hawks Up At Your Class Photo
cards.title: Hawks Up At Your Class Photo
cards.subtitle: Entering-class photo ritual
cards.notes: Join the entering-class photo during orientation and use the linked-thumbs Hawks Up hand sign when the photographer calls for it.
cards.short_summary: The first class portrait pairs a Seattle U welcome photo with the Redhawk hand sign.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists Hawks Up at the class photo as a new-student tradition and publishes instructions for the gesture.
cards.access_notes: Class-photo timing is part of Orientation programming; follow staff directions onsite.

cards.title: Winter Ball
cards.subtitle: SEAC annual dance
cards.notes: Watch ConnectSU and SEAC announcements for the venue and dress guidance, then plan a group photo around the featured cultural setting.
cards.short_summary: A Student Events and Activities Council annual dance held at Seattle cultural venues.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes Winter Ball as a fun annual SU dance run by the Student Events and Activities Council.
cards.access_notes: Venue and event details vary by year; check ConnectSU or SEAC announcements.

cards.title: New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Fall-quarter academic ceremony
cards.notes: Put this opening ceremony on your Fall Welcome calendar and listen for the president, provost, and student-body president remarks.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s first academic ceremony formally marks the beginning of a new student’s journey.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University calls New Student Convocation an important rite of passage and the first SU academic ceremony for new students.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled during Fall Welcome; consult the current Welcome Events schedule.

cards.title: Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Annual fall-quarter observance
cards.notes: If this observance fits your interests, check Campus Ministry’s fall schedule and attend at Immaculate Conception Church with the campus community.
cards.short_summary: A fall-quarter blessing for the new academic year, rooted in Catholic university practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University holds an annual Mass of the Holy Spirit at Immaculate Conception Church to seek blessings on the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Annual fall-quarter event; participation is open across religious, secular, and spiritual identities.

cards.title: New Student Retreat
cards.subtitle: Campus Ministry fall-quarter tradition
cards.notes: Apply through Campus Ministry early in fall if you want a small-group setting to reflect, meet peers, and begin the quarter together.
cards.short_summary: A fall retreat specifically designed to help first-year and transfer students build community.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes New Student Retreat as a fall-quarter Seattle U tradition for first-year and transfer undergraduates.
cards.access_notes: Offered by Campus Ministry each fall quarter; registration details are announced by Campus Ministry.

cards.title: Christmas Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Annual campus holiday gathering
cards.notes: Arrive for Student Center activities, then head outside for the lighting, chapel choir carols, and Redhawk mascot appearance.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s annual seasonal gathering combines indoor festivities with an outdoor tree-lighting ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes an annual Christmas Tree Lighting with Student Center festivities, chapel choir carols, and Rudy the Redhawk.
cards.access_notes: Annual seasonal program; verify the current date and activity details through student-event listings.

cards.title: International Dinner
cards.subtitle: International Student Center winter-quarter event
cards.notes: Look for winter-quarter registration details and come ready to watch cultural performances while learning from student organizers and community partners.
cards.short_summary: A student-organized dinner and performance program connecting campus cultures with the Seattle community.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University calls International Dinner a historic annual winter-quarter event, entirely student-organized, with food and cultural performances.
cards.access_notes: Hosted every winter quarter by the International Student Center; confirm the current event listing.

cards.title: Quadstock
cards.subtitle: SEAC annual music festival
cards.notes: Check SEAC’s spring announcements for the lineup and event rules, then plan to spend the day at this campus music-festival tradition.
cards.short_summary: An all-day annual music festival organized by the Student Events and Activities Council.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University describes Quadstock as SEAC’s annual, all-day music festival event.
cards.access_notes: Annual spring-quarter event; lineup, schedule, and access details change each year.
